thread:
raj: Heads-up — noticed an ECC correctable spike in us-west-gpu-pool since 16:12. 3 GPUs crossed ~10/hr. Some Xid 13/31 showing up intermittently. Proposing we revisit auto-drain policy (hysteresis + flaky vs failing classification). CC @amy @mike
sre-bot: ALERT: ECC_CORRECTABLE_RATE HIGH on us-west-gpu-pool — 3 GPUs >10/hr. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/GPUpool
amy: Can you paste the prom query and current thresholds? IIRC we set auto-drain at 50/hr last quarter
raj: Prom query I used: ```sum by(gpu_id) (increase(nvidia_ecc_correctable_total[1h]))``` Current policy: auto-drain when any gpu >50 correctables in 1h OR Xid_errors >=3 in 5m. That's been noisy on old cards. Thinking: add debounce (sustained 15m), classify single-bit vs multi-bit if possible, and only auto-drain on multi-bit/Xid streamers
mike: IMO increase correctable threshold to 100/hr and require sustained >threshold for 15m before drain. Also treat Xid 13/31 as medium-severity — only drain if Xid count keeps rising after soft-reset. For outright immediate drain, require Xid >=5 in 10m or evidence of memory ECC multi-bit
taylor: We should also have a short playbook for operators: 1) pull NVML logs (nvidia-smi --query-ecc...), 2) try `sudo nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <gpu>` if supported, 3) cordon instance and reprovision if still noisy after 1 reboot/hour, 4) mark for RMA if memtest fails. Document these steps in KB.
jen: Note capacity/cost tradeoff — draining reduces usable GPUs. We should limit auto-drain to dedicated/reserved pools only. For spot/preemptible pools, escalate to on-call but don't auto-drain unless Xid storm (preempt risk is already high).
amy: Proposal: keep alerting for correctable-only (pager to infra on-call but no automatic drain). Auto-drain only on (a) Xid >=5 within 10m, (b) multi-bit ECC detected, or (c) correctable >200/hr sustained for 30m. Roll out behind a feature flag and run canary in staging/us-west-staging for 48h.
raj: Sounds good. I'll set a short experiment: apply new rules to us-west-staging pool first. Config snippet for feature flag + policy: ```auto_drain: enabled: false feature_flag: ecc_autodrain_v2 canary_pools: ["us-west-staging"] rules: - type: xid immediate_threshold: 5 window: 10m action: drain - type: correctable sustained_threshold: 200 window: 30m debounce: 15m action: drain - type: correctable alert_threshold: 20 window: 15m action: notify```
mike: I'll open PR with the feature flag, prometheus rules, and a small operator UI tweak to show 'drain risk' score. Also adding metrics: `gpu_correctable_sustained_count`, `gpu_xid_rate`, `auto_drain_trigger_count`.
taylor: Also recommend adding weekly memtest job for pools with >10 unique GPUs hitting correctables in a week. Helps catch early-degradation cards before they blow up.
amy: sgtm :thumbsup:
raj: Action items: 1) mike -> PR for flag + Prom rules + metrics (assigning to you) 2) raj -> create INFRA ticket with NVML logs & attach Grafana links 3) taylor -> draft playbook KB steps and memtest job 4) jen -> add gating: only enable auto-drain for dedicated pools. For current spike: no auto-drain unless Xid >=5 or sustained >200/hr. I'll hold manual drain for now and monitor.
mike: PR created draft at https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452 — runbook and tests pending.
raj: Created INFRA-1287 and added screenshots + nvml output. Will monitor for next 2h and escalate to paging if thresholds hit. Closing thread here but will post updates to the ticket.
jen: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage.
raj: Thanks all.
